rationale: I read only the authoritative source PDF (pages 1-3, extracted with pdftotext), the source contract, the blind translation, the core semantic checklist, and the output schema; I read no Lean, no dossier, and no other audit artifact. Applying the authoritative module definability convention: because the first edition defines E X as a Lebesgue integral (footnote 1, printed page 5) without any exceptional-value convention for arbitrary real random variables, each ordinary real-valued E X is read on its finite-integral domain, so integrability of X and of φ ∘ X are part of the configured source contract for this module and are not to be scored as reduced applicability; only restrictions beyond those declared definability conditions would be not-faithful-weaker. All twelve checks were completed in order: C01-C08 and C10-C12 pass on direct evidence, and C09 is not-applicable for the concrete reason that the selected result contains no constants, coefficients, exponents, indices, or ranges on either side. Substantively, the translation reproduces the printed display exactly: two universal binders over one non-strict inequality; the ambient probability space made explicit with total mass 1 per footnote 1; φ typed ℝ → ℝ and convex on all of ℝ, which is precisely footnote 3's convexity over the whole domain rather than the sharper convex-subset form; the left side φ applied to the scalar integral of X and the right side the integral of the composite φ ∘ X, honouring footnote 2's binding convention; and, for ℝ-valued functions, the Bochner integral of the anonymized LocalDef001 coincides with footnote 1's Lebesgue integral. The dependency ledger interprets every nontrivial constant from its declaration (notably LocalDef001, MeasureTheory.integral, ConvexOn, Integrable, IsProbabilityMeasure, Set.univ) rather than from its name, with the remaining entries correctly identified as instance plumbing fixing ℝ's standard norm, topology, order, and scalar multiplication. Both implications hold: instantiating the translation at the contract's data yields the printed inequality, and the contract's statement applies verbatim to any data satisfying the translation's hypotheses. The only asymmetries are widenings (a.e. strong measurability rather than strict measurability) or apparent strengthenings that the contract's undebatable constraints resolve in the translation's favour (convexity on all of ℝ is the printed hypothesis). Two remarks in the blind translation — that convexity on Set.univ is 'strictly stronger' and that assuming hφX 'weakens the conclusion's scope' — are artefacts of judging blind against the sharpest textbook Jensen rather than against Vershynin's sentence and this module's policy; both are resolved on the evidence above and neither leaves unresolved evidence. Classification: faithful-equivalent; accepted; no adjudication required.
